discipline_framing: The rates and currencies discipline of the futures fundamental analyst — Federal Reserve operations, global yield curves, fixed-income mathematics, and international trade balances as the force field within which every other futures complex prices, and a primary trading domain in its own right
audience: Fundamental analysts of futures markets who need dedicated command of rate and currency complexes: Fed and central-bank operations, global curve analysis, fixed-income mathematics, FX market structure and flows, and the trade-balance systems connecting currencies to the real economy
sources: The Federal Reserve operational literature (the implementation frameworks from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, the post-2008 and post-2020 operating-system changes, the FOMC communication and SEP documentation)
The fixed-income analytics canon (the Tuckman Bond-Markets-Strategies-and-Tools tradition, the Fabozzi handbook lineage, the duration-convexity and curve-arithmetic discipline)
The term-structure research (the expectations-hypothesis tests, the term-premium estimation tradition including the ACM and Kim-Wright models, the yield-curve and recession literature)

The international finance canon (the parity-conditions literature, the exchange-rate-determination research from monetary through balance-of-payments approaches, the Krugman-Obstfeld textbook tradition)
The FX market structure literature (the BIS triennial survey tradition, the flow and positioning research, the carry-trade and crash literature from the Brunnermeier-Nagel-Vayanos lineage)
The central-bank policy research (the inflation-targeting history, the unconventional-policy evaluations from QE through yield-curve control, the divergence and spillover studies)
The global dollar system literature (the cross-currency basis research, the EME vulnerability frameworks from the BIS tradition, the safe-haven and reserve-currency studies)
pitfalls: Level-versus-change confusion — quoting rates and curve positions without the change dynamics that actually generate futures P-and-L, positioning on levels the market priced months ago
Single-central-bank tunnel vision — analyzing Fed policy in isolation while global curve linkages, divergence trades, and spillover flows drive the actual moves
Parity-violation naivety — treating PPP or UIP deviations as arbitrage opportunities rather than the documented risk-premium and constraint phenomena they represent
Duration-blind sizing — expressing rate views through instruments whose DV01, convexity, and option features were never computed, discovering leverage through losses
Trade-balance mechanical reading — forecasting FX from trade-flow arithmetic while capital flows, policy divergence, and positioning dominate the actual price formation
